newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tatneft to place by mid-year.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tatneft to place by mid-year.

text.p: Regional Russian oil company AO Tatneft will present a Eurobond issue prospectus to the government of the autonomous republic of Tatarstan on February 15 and will start placing the bonds by the middle of 1997, a finance ministry official said on Friday.
"I cannot mention the sum, since the prospectus is not yet approved, but we are talking about millions of dollars," head of securities department Konstantin Kolesnik told Reuters.
Previously Tatarstan Prime Minister Farid Mukhamedshin has said that the volume will be $200 to $300 million.
Kolesnik said the Eurobonds would be repaid in 1999 or 2000.
The Tatar Finance Ministry planned to appoint Tatneft's financial adviser Solid lead-manager by March 15, and Moscow bank Zenit underwriter of the issue, Kolesnik said.

Last July Tatneft issued level-one American Depositary Receipts (ADRs). In December it placed American Depositary Shares covering 10 percent of its authorised capital among institutional investors. It is considering issuing level-three ADRs in 1997.
With annual output in 1996 of 23.70 million tonnes, it is one of Russia's biggest oil companies.

Tatneft's authorised capital is 232.62 billion roubles. It major shareholders are the Tatar government with about 32 percent and employees with 41.34 percent. Foreign investors have 11.6 percent of shares and Tatneft's suppliers have 3.66 percent.
Kolesnik said other oil companies in Tatarstan were preparing Eurobond issues this year.

"The documents for Kazanorgsintez, Kazanneftekhim and other companies' Eurobond issues are now being prepared," he said. "By June we are to privatise the companies and prepare to place their paper on the Western market."
